chunks: Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman narrated, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father, from his grandfather, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Four [groups] on whose behalf I will intercede on the Day of Resurrection, even if they were given the sins of the people of the earth: Those who assist my Household, those who fulfill their needs when they are in need of them, those who love them with their heart and tongue, and those who defend them with their hand.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four groups for whom the Prophet will intercede on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* emphasizes the concept of *al-wala'* (loyalty) to the Ahl al-Bayt as a prerequisite for the Prophet’s intercession (*shafa'ah*), highlighting that love and assistance are not merely emotional but involve active support. It underscores the Shia theological view that the Prophet’s authority extends to guiding the faithful through his progeny, linking spiritual devotion with practical defense of the Imams. The narration reinforces the idea that true faith is manifested through both heart and hand in relation to the Ahl al-Bayt.
